content:
The image shows a corn leaf with:
- Numerous small, dark reddish-brown to black raised pustules scattered densely across the leaf surface
- Pustules appear on what looks like the upper leaf surface
- Surrounding tissue shows yellowing/chlorosis
- Some larger coalescing dark/necrotic areas
- Pustules are small, circular to oval in shape
- Very dense, uniform distribution of small dark pustules

Key distinctions:
- The pustules are small, circular, densely packed, and appear primarily on the upper leaf surface — this matches **Southern Rust** (not Common Rust, which has larger, more elongated pustules on both surfaces)
- Southern Rust pustules are smaller, more circular, more densely packed, lighter orange to cinnamon-red, and found almost exclusively on the upper leaf surface
- Common Rust pustules are larger, more elongated, and occur on both leaf surfaces

The dense, small, circular dark pustules predominantly on the upper surface strongly point to Southern Rust.
